findings.title: The biggest IT search in the home city returns ten companies and none is VAF
findings.evidence: "Managed it services indianapolis" is 1,000 searches a month at difficulty 29. Asked from Indianapolis, the top ten are leapmanagedit.com, cloudtango.net, gadellnet.com, mis.tech, meriplex.com, exactitconsulting.com, esi.tech, visualedgeit.com, revenuebase.ai and corsicatech.com. The page that should win it, /information/managed-it-services, is one of the best on the site at 86 of 100 with 1,070 words, five question headings and FAQPage markup. The same template in Fort Wayne ranks 6 and 4 for its city terms.
findings.impact: The single largest managed IT search in the market VAF is headquartered in sends every click, and every AI answer built on those results, to ten other providers.
findings.action: Rebuild /indianapolis/ and /information/managed-it-services as one linked pair with Service schema, an FAQPage block on cost and scope, and named Indianapolis proof. Link both from the home page and from all 35 city pages.

findings.title: Copier leasing in Indianapolis is invisible in both search results and AI answers
findings.evidence: Asked from Indianapolis, "copier lease indianapolis" returns visualedgeit.com, werentcopiers.com, copierleaseindianapolis.com, copierleasecenter.com, gflesch.com, hartfordrents.com, bbb.org, iccbusinessproducts.com and leapcopierprinter.com, with no VAF. Claude answered the same question after reading ten sources and vanausdall.com was not one. /copiers/ is the strongest page on the site at 96 of 100 with FAQPage and Service schema, so the content exists and nothing points it at the lease query.
findings.impact: Copier leasing is the oldest line and the door into print, phones and IT contracts, and the answer engines are handing that door to ICC, Visual Edge and two lease microsites.
findings.action: Extend /copiers/ with lease terms, cost ranges and the lease questions buyers ask, and give it an Indianapolis heading and title. Claim the directory listings that rank for the term.

findings.title: Four of every five organic visits come from people who already know the name
findings.evidence: Semrush records 373 organic keywords and 1,081 visits a month, worth about $960 in equivalent paid traffic. Branded share is 80 percent, and five brand phrases take 79.9 percent of the traffic between them. The home page alone accounts for 85.56 percent of site traffic on 32 keywords, while /indianapolis/ appears nowhere in the top pages list.
findings.impact: The site is a business card for existing customers, not a source of new ones. Almost no one who does not already know VAF arrives through search.
findings.action: The nine money pages get service and city targeting so non-brand demand has somewhere to land, and branded share is reported monthly.

findings.title: The site is not written in the shape an answer engine can quote
findings.evidence: Answer-shaped content scored 21 of 100, the lowest component on the scorecard. FAQ marked up as FAQPage appears on 4 of 110 service, industry and location pages, question headings on 23 of 110, and Service or Article schema on 3 of 113 buyer and blog pages. The assistants already know the name: asked six buyer questions, Claude named VAF in five and cited vanausdall.com in four, never as the first recommendation. On managed IT it named the company and then drew on 29 sources, none of them yours. Cyber security was the one answer that neither named nor cited the company.
findings.impact: When a buyer asks an assistant who to call in Indianapolis, VAF is named once in five. The named companies get the shortlist.
findings.action: Every money page gets three to six real buyer questions as H2s with short answers and FAQPage markup, plus Service schema naming the service and the area served. /copiers/ and /copier-service-repair are the template.

findings.title: No review markup anywhere, and the reviews search is owned by job sites
findings.evidence: Review or AggregateRating schema is absent on all 171 pages. /about/customer-comments carries 20 words and scores 43 of 100. "Van ausdall & farrar reviews" asked from Indianapolis returns indeed.com in four positions, glassdoor.com in three, facebook.com and yelp.com, with vanausdall.com in none. gflesch.com, visualedgeit.com, appliedinnovation.com and bradenonline.com carry no review markup either.
findings.impact: A buyer checking VAF reads what former staff said about working there rather than what customers say about the service, and the engines have no rating to attach to the company.
findings.action: Collect customer reviews on Google, rebuild /about/customer-comments with Review markup, and pull three onto each money page. This is the one signal no competitor in this market has.

findings.title: Authority is a third of the market's and almost half the links come from one site
findings.evidence: Authority Score is 21 of 100 from 510 referring domains and 2,687 backlinks, against a competitor median of 1,211 referring domains: visualedgeit.com 2,353, gflesch.com 1,656, appliedinnovation.com 1,190, bradenonline.com 1,171. Only 41 of the 510 domains score 30 or better. One domain, indianaruralhealth.org, is the source of 45.6 percent of every link to the site, and 46.5 percent of links carry no anchor text because they are logos.
findings.impact: Low authority is why a good page such as /information/managed-it-services loses Indianapolis terms it wins in Fort Wayne, and one lapsed relationship would take nearly half the link profile with it.
findings.action: Fifteen new Indianapolis-area referring domains in 90 days from chambers, associations, customers, suppliers and sponsorships, and ask logo-linking partners for the company name in the image alt text.

findings.title: The Indianapolis page is long enough to rank and built like a brochure
findings.evidence: /indianapolis/ runs 1,102 words and scores 66 of 100, but it has zero question headings, no FAQPage and no Service schema, and it does not appear in the Semrush top pages list at all. Across all 35 city pages, none carries FAQ or Service schema. The Fort Wayne and Evansville managed IT pages, which do carry question headings, are the only city pages earning measurable traffic, at 2.03 and 0.92 percent.
findings.impact: The page that should be the hub for the headquarters city earns nothing and passes no strength to the Indianapolis service pages.
findings.action: Rebuild /indianapolis/ as a hub with a service list linking to all nine money pages, two named local case studies, six FAQ questions in FAQPage markup and Service schema for each line.

findings.title: Ten location pages are too thin to say anything, including the two markets with demand
findings.evidence: Twenty-five of 35 location pages clear the word threshold and ten do not: /columbus/ at 120 words, /south-bend/ at 119, /bloomington/ at 129, /muncie/ at 122, /carmel/ at 123, /fishers/ at 131, /greenwood/ at 126 and /noblesville/ at 121. Two of those towns have measured demand: "copiers columbus" is 40 a month with VAF absent from the top ten, and "copiers south bend" is 10 a month where VAF sits at 2.
findings.impact: Columbus buyers get an Ohio result set and no VAF, and the thin suburb pages give an assistant nothing to quote when it is asked who serves those towns.
findings.action: Rebuild /columbus/ and /south-bend/ first on the location template with services, a local proof point, FAQPage markup and Service schema, then the remaining eight.

findings.title: The phone systems page ranks third on a page that skips every answer signal
findings.evidence: /communication/business-phone-systems is 568 words, scores 66 of 100, and has no question headings, no FAQPage and no Service schema. It ranks 3 for "business phone systems indianapolis" (30 a month) and 5 for "voip phone systems indianapolis" (50 a month at difficulty 1). This is also the one query where Claude named VAF. The Fort Wayne version ranks 25 for the national term "business phone systems", 9,900 a month.
findings.impact: The page is already close and the two easiest lifts on the site, difficulty 1 and difficulty 0 city terms, sit at 5 and 3 instead of 1.
findings.action: Add six buyer questions with FAQPage markup, Service schema, a hosted voice comparison and the Indianapolis proof that supports the claim.

findings.title: The cyber security page names no city, asks no question and carries no service markup
findings.evidence: /cyber-security-solutions runs 662 words and scores 58 of 100, with no city in the title, zero question headings, no FAQPage and no Service schema. "Cyber security services indianapolis" is 10 a month and VAF is in none of the top ten. Claude read 16 sources answering the same question and used none from vanausdall.com. Meanwhile the Fort Wayne managed IT page ranks 8 for "cybersecurity services fort wayne indiana", 170 a month.
findings.impact: Security is the service buyers most often ask an assistant to recommend, and VAF is not in the source set the assistant reads.
findings.action: Rewrite with Indianapolis in the title and H1, question headings on cost, scope and compliance, FAQPage and Service schema, and links to /network-security and /information/managed-it-services.

findings.title: Sixty-five pages are too short to compete and fifty-nine grade D or F
findings.evidence: Across 171 pages the average is 463 words and 65 sit under 300; 59 pages grade D or F and only three grade A. In the money set, /communication/call-recording is 72 words, /communication/unified-communications 84, /network-infrastructure 105 and /it-support 187 despite targeting "Indianapolis IT Support" in its title. The three A pages, /copiers/ at 96, /copier-service-repair at 91 and /copy-print-solutions/ at 86, are the only ones carrying FAQ, Service schema and question headings together.
findings.impact: Two thirds of the site adds no ranking or answering value, and it dilutes the strength the good pages need.
findings.action: Merge the sub-100-word feature pages into their parent service pages, rebuild /it-support on the /copiers/ template, and produce a keep, merge or retire list for the rest.

findings.title: Three blog posts, none marked up, yet the blog is already ranking
findings.evidence: The crawl found three posts at a median of 589 words, none with Article schema and none with FAQ markup, though two of three answer a question outright. The physical intrusion detection post is the second highest traffic page on the whole site, carrying 4.16 percent of organic traffic and ranking 6 for its term at 110 a month. Two document conversion posts rank 2 and 7 for terms at 70 and 140 a month, outranking the service page. All of them sit on query-string URLs of the form /blog?p=, and the sitemap lists 325 such URLs.
findings.impact: The one part of the site that earns non-brand rankings has no markup, so it cannot be quoted as an article by an answer engine, and a crawler following links reaches three of the 325.
findings.action: Move posts to clean paths under /blog/ with 301s and Article schema, then publish two posts a month against the measured questions, starting with what managed IT services cost at 720 a month.

findings.title: Crawling and access are clean, with one file missing and no breadcrumbs anywhere
findings.evidence: Crawlability scored 100 of 100: robots.txt readable, one sitemap, HTTPS, canonical tags correct on 171 of 171 pages, no accidental noindex, 171 of 171 URLs answering. All eight crawlers checked are allowed, including GPTBot, ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, CCBot and Google-Extended, giving 94 of 100 for AI access against visualedgeit.com at 100. The gap is llms.txt, which is not published. BreadcrumbList schema appears on 0 of 171 pages, and 4 of 141 meta descriptions fall outside a usable length.
findings.impact: Nothing is being blocked, so this is housekeeping rather than lost customers, but breadcrumbs and llms.txt are two free signals competitors have started to use.
findings.action: Publish llms.txt listing the money pages and the entity facts, add BreadcrumbList schema sitewide, and correct the four meta descriptions.

why_beaten.intro: Each company's Indianapolis money page was parsed the same way on 15 September 2026, alongside the Semrush link figures and the live result set asked from Indianapolis. For Van Ausdall & Farrar the page measured is /indianapolis/.
rows: FAQPage schema on the money page
Service schema on the money page
Position for managed print services Indianapolis, 170 a month
why_beaten.verdict: Nobody in this market has FAQ, Service or Review markup on their Indianapolis page, so the answer-shaped signals are open ground rather than catch-up. What separates the leaders is authority and depth: visualedgeit.com wins managed print with 628 words and 2,353 referring domains, gflesch.com with 1,314 words and 1,656. The pattern to copy is one page per city per service, built on VAF's own /copiers/ template, which already scores 96 and is the only page type on the site carrying all three markup types.

leverage.intro: The five moves with the biggest return for the least effort, in the order we would do them. Each is either in the build or in the first 30 to 90 days of the plan.

items.move: Rebuild the Indianapolis pair around managed IT
items.payoff: "Managed it services indianapolis" is 1,000 a month at difficulty 29 and VAF is in none of the top ten. The page that should win it already scores 81 with 1,070 words, five question headings and FAQPage markup, and the identical Fort Wayne page ranks 4 and 6 for its city terms, so the format is proven and only the Indianapolis targeting and internal linking are missing. This one term is larger than every other Indianapolis query measured put together.

items.move: Roll the /copiers/ template across the other eight money pages
items.payoff: /copiers/ scores 96, /copier-service-repair 91 and /copy-print-solutions/ 86, and they are the only pages carrying question headings, FAQPage and Service schema together. The others are missing all three: cyber security 58, IT support 56 at 187 words, network security 66, document management 66, phone systems 66. The phone systems page is first in the queue because it already ranks 3 and 5 for two city terms at difficulty 0 and 1.

items.move: Get listed where the engines and the buyers look
items.payoff: cloudtango.net ranks 2 for managed IT in Indianapolis and was one of the sources Claude read. goodfirms.co ranks 1 for cyber security in the city, bbb.org ranks 7 for copier leasing, and clutch.co, builtin.com, expertise.com and chamberofcommerce.com all appear in the source sets. VAF is listed in none of them. This is the fastest route into AI answers VAF does not currently appear in.

items.move: Collect customer reviews and publish them with markup
items.payoff: Review schema is absent on all 171 pages, and on all four competitors' Indianapolis pages, so this is the one differentiating signal available. Today "van ausdall & farrar reviews" returns nothing but Indeed, Glassdoor, Facebook and Yelp, so a buyer researching VAF reads employee opinions instead of customer ones.

items.move: Earn 15 local referring domains and reduce the single-source risk
items.payoff: Authority Score 21 from 510 referring domains against a competitor median of 1,211, with indianaruralhealth.org alone accounting for 45.6 percent of all links and a further 46.5 percent carrying no anchor text because they are logos. Low authority is the reason a strong page wins Fort Wayne terms and loses the identical Indianapolis ones.

blog.intro: 324 posts, sampled 40 at random and parsed the same way as the pages. The blog is the most consistent thing VAF publishes and the least marked up.
stats: posts in the sitemap, all on blog?p= query-string URLs
posts in 2024, 2025 and 2026 so far: about one a week
median words per post; only 4 of 40 sampled were under 400
posts with BlogPosting or Article schema, a published date or an author in the markup
findings: Cadence is the asset. About one post a week for three years is more than any Indiana competitor publishes. Leap's blog subfolder is minor in its traffic; VAF's second-highest traffic URL is a blog post.

Nothing tells an engine these are articles. No BlogPosting schema, no datePublished, no author, no visible date on the page. An assistant cannot judge freshness or authorship, which is what it weighs for how-to and cost questions.

Titles already ask questions ('How does content management make office procedures more productive?', 'What are data backup and recovery services?'). The first paragraph rarely answers them in one sentence, so there is nothing to lift into an AI answer.
URLs are query strings (blog?p=slug-YYMMDD). Google indexes them, but they carry no folder signal, cannot be grouped by pillar, and make 55 percent of the sitemap look like duplicates of one page.

Document conversion posts rank 2 to 7 for 'document conversion companies' and 'document conversion service' with no schema at all. That is what the rest of the blog could do with markup and internal links.
actions: Build
BlogPosting schema on every post with datePublished, dateModified, author as a Person and the pillar as articleSection. The build's post template does this.
Build
Move to /blog/pillar/slug/ with a 301 from every blog?p= URL. The redirect map is generated from the sitemap.
Build
Answer-first rewrite of the top 30 posts by traffic: a one-sentence answer under the H1, a five-question FAQ marked up as FAQPage, and three links into the service page the post supports.
30 days
Author pages for the people who write: Person schema, role, credentials, LinkedIn as sameAs. Authorship is a ranking input for advice content.
Ongoing
Keep the weekly cadence, but pick topics from the question keyword pulls (720 to 1,000 searches a month) instead of vendor news, and refresh the top 30 every six months with a new dateModified.

social.intro: Answer engines corroborate a company across the web before they name it. VAF's profiles exist and some are active, but nothing on the site connects them, and video is split across two channels nobody can find.
stats: LinkedIn company followers; the COO's personal profile has about 2,000
YouTube subscribers on the linked channel; 16 videos, top video 78 views; a second unlisted-looking channel also exists
sameAs links in the Organization schema; no logo, no description, no foundingDate either
Facebook posts link back to blog posts; Instagram is linked from the footer
findings: The Organization schema is an empty shell: type and address, nothing else. Without sameAs, an engine has to guess that the LinkedIn page, the Facebook page, the YouTube channels and the Crunchbase profile are the same entity as vanausdall.com. Both competitors' schema is richer.

YouTube is the most under-used channel. Seven site pages embed videos, but the channel is not linked from the site, has two identities, and the videos carry no VideoObject schema, so none of that watch time or transcript text counts toward the brand.

Individuals outrank the company. The COO's profile has more followers than the company page. Employee posts that repeat the site's FAQ answers, word for word, are the cheapest corroboration available.
No Google Business Profile appeared in the brand reviews search. For a three-office dealer, GBP posts, Q&A and reviews are the single largest local AEO input and are not being fed.

Facebook is the only channel that links to the blog. LinkedIn should carry the same posts with the same answer sentence, since LinkedIn is indexed and quoted by assistants far more often than Facebook.
actions: Build

Organization schema with sameAs to LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Crunchbase and BBB, plus logo, description, foundingDate 1914, numberOfEmployees, areaServed and the three offices as LocalBusiness subOrganizations.
Build
One YouTube channel, linked from the footer, every embedded video wrapped in VideoObject schema with a transcript. Upload the existing customer testimonial and assessment videos there.
30 days
Claim and complete the Google Business Profile for all three offices: services, Q&A seeded with the site FAQ, weekly posts, review requests after every service ticket closes.
30 days
A LinkedIn cadence that mirrors the blog: one post a week, first line is the answer sentence from the post, link to the post. Three employees reshare with a sentence of their own.
90 days

Get listed where assistants look: Clutch, Cloudtango, the Indy Chamber directory and vendor partner locators (Canon, Ricoh, Kyocera, Mitel, Fortinet). Each is a citation with the same name, address and phone as the site.
